name: Host Hotels & Resorts

logo.source: commons.wikimedia.org (Logo Host Hotels & Resorts.svg); no logo in the Wikipedia infobox

description: Host Hotels & Resorts is the largest publicly traded lodging REIT: it owns 76 mostly luxury and upper-upscale hotels (about 41,700 rooms) as of February 20, 2026, and books the hotels' full revenue, not a fee. Guests pay for rooms, food and beverage, spas, parking and resort fees at the hotel; independent managers (Marriott, Hyatt, Hilton, Accor and others) run every hotel day to day under management agreements and are paid a fee, so Host carries the building, the renovation bills and the swings in occupancy and rates. About 63 percent of 2025 hotel revenue came from Marriott-family brands. Host sells hotels when it can get good prices (about $1.1 billion for two Four Seasons resorts in February 2026) and passes taxable gains to shareholders as special dividends. It also built and sold Four Seasons-branded condominiums next to its Orlando resort, a one-off real estate sales line.

hq.note: 4747 Bethesda Avenue, Suite 1300, Bethesda, MD 20814 (SEC submissions record). Files a combined 10-K with subsidiary Host Hotels & Resorts, L.P. (CIK 0001061937), the operating partnership.

employees.note: 162 employees, all in the US (FY2025 10-K). Excludes hotel staff: third-party managers hire and direct the workforce at the hotels. Three Brazil hotels' staff are technically Host employees but supervised by the local manager.

businessLines.name: Rooms
businessLines.shareBasis: 3,608 / 6,114 total revenues, computed from FY2025 10-K note 16
businessLines.how: Guests (transient leisure and business travellers, groups, contract blocks such as airline crews) pay a nightly rate to stay; revenue is rooms available times occupancy times average rate, and Host takes it all before paying the manager a fee and the hotel's costs.
businessLines.description: Room-night revenue from the owned hotels, part of the single Hotel Ownership segment.

operatingProfit.note: Computed: rooms revenue $3,608M less rooms departmental expense $906M (10-K note 16); this is before management fees, property-level costs and depreciation, not an operating profit

businessLines.name: Food and beverage
businessLines.how: Guests and groups pay per meal, drink, banquet or meeting package at the hotel; group business brings large catering orders.
businessLines.description: Restaurants, lounges, banquets and meeting-room catering at the owned hotels.

operatingProfit.note: Computed: F&B revenue $1,803M less F&B departmental expense $1,224M; before shared costs

businessLines.name: Other hotel revenue
businessLines.how: Guests pay per service or charge (spa treatments, parking, resort fees, other outlets) on top of the room.
businessLines.description: Spa, parking, resort and other ancillary fees, plus other income at the hotels.

businessLines.name: Condominium sales (Four Seasons Orlando residences)
businessLines.how: One-time sale of each condominium unit to a buyer; revenue stops when the units are sold out.
businessLines.description: Sales of 40 Four Seasons-branded condominium units and villas built on a five-acre parcel next to the Four Seasons Resort Orlando at Walt Disney World. Construction was completed in Q2 2026.

revenue.note: 16 units sold in 2025, $17M net income recognised (10-K MD&A); $79M in H1 2026 ($53M in Q2) from four units in Q1 and seven villas in Q2 (10-Q Q2 2026)

businessLines.revenueNote: 16 units sold in 2025, $17M net income recognised (10-K MD&A); $79M in H1 2026 ($53M in Q2) from four units in Q1 and seven villas in Q2 (10-Q Q2 2026)

brands.name: Marriott family (Marriott, Ritz-Carlton, JW Marriott, Westin, W, Luxury Collection, Sheraton, AC, Autograph, Tribute)
brands.share: 48 hotels, 28,371 rooms, 62.9% of FY2025 hotel revenues
brands.note: Largest: Marriott 25 hotels 18,579 rooms 35.3%; Ritz-Carlton 6 hotels 12.2%; Westin 7 hotels 6.9%

brands.name: Hyatt family (Grand Hyatt, Hyatt Regency, Andaz, Alila, Hyatt Place)
brands.share: 13 hotels, 8,313 rooms, 16.5% of FY2025 hotel revenues

brands.name: Sold hotels
brands.share: 6% of FY2025 hotel revenues (10-K table footnote)

brands.name: Geographic concentration
brands.share: New York, Washington DC, San Diego, San Francisco, Phoenix, Florida and Hawaii together were about 65% of FY2025 hotel revenues; five hotels in Brazil and Canada were about 2%; no single hotel above 6%

brands.name: Managers
brands.share: About 89% of rooms are managed by the brand's own manager; 11% by independent managers under franchise or independent-brand agreements (10-K)

whatsNext.text: 2026 capital expenditures of $525M to $625M: ROI projects about $250M to $300M and renewal and replacement $275M to $325M; includes finishing the Hyatt transformation program (three properties in 2026) and starting a Marriott program at four properties over four years.
2026 comparable hotel RevPAR growth guided to 2.0% to 3.5%
